components.description: A quieter choice beside a primary action, such as Change the date.

components.css: .ds-tabs { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 78px); border-top: 1px solid var(--line-soft, #dcd8ce); background: var(--nav-surface, #f6f3ea); } .ds-tabs a { position: relative; display: flex; min-height: 76px; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 3px; padding: 12px 2px 14px; color: var(--nav-inactive, #676964); font: 500 11.5px/1.15 'Noto Sans', sans-serif; font-stretch: 87.5%; text-decoration: none; } .ds-tabs a:hover, .ds-tabs a.is-active { color: var(--nav-active, #24362b); } .ds-tabs a.is-active { font-weight: 650; } .ds-tabs a.is-active::after { position: absolute; bottom: 18px; left: 50%; width: 42px; height: 3px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--accent-line, #a9804a); content: ''; transform: translateX(-50%); }

narrative.overview:
Every day starts under a forest at first light. A dark band painted with mist, ridgelines, pines and a low sun holds everything about the chapter: its name, its theme, the campaign day and the days left to the trial. Below it the page turns to warm paper, and the day's work is set out as a plain board of orders. Readiness comes first, because it decides what the day can hold. Then come the main order, the two watches and the Hearth mission.

The system is quiet and legible. The painting is the only picture, and gold is the only accent, used sparingly. Type does the rest: a sturdy book serif names chapters, headings and numbers, and a narrow humanist sans carries everything a person reads or taps. Surfaces are flat. Hierarchy comes from the dark-to-paper step, hairline borders and type weight, never from shadows. The app is used on a phone before training and in low light at the watches, so touch targets stay large and the dark variant follows the phone.

The world was chosen as "Forest Light". The Road page borrows the "Night Atlas" route line: a winding trail with a gold Today mark and a ring for the trial.
keyCharacteristics: One painted forest band per screen that has one, with its text set directly on it.
Warm paper ground with 1px borders and small radii.
Gold as a single accent: the pine mark, the theme line, the main order's top edge, the selected tab.
Wittgenstein for names and numbers; Noto Sans at a semi-condensed width for UI.
Readiness named in words, with color only repeating it.

rules.name: The One Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold marks identity and progress only: the pine mark, the chapter theme, the main order's top edge, the selected tab, and the route's Today mark and trial ring. It never fills a card or a paragraph.

rules.name: The Words First Rule
rules.body: A readiness state is always named in words. The tint only repeats what the words say, so the state reads correctly without color.

rules.name: The Serif Names, Sans Works Rule
rules.body: Wittgenstein is for names, headings and numbers. Anything a person reads as instructions or taps is set in Noto Sans.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces on paper use a border or a tint to separate, never a shadow.

dos: **Do** give every control a tap area at least 48px tall (the `--touch-target` token). A control may draw smaller only when its tap area still reaches 48px.
**Do** name each readiness state in words and let its tint repeat it.
**Do** keep gold to the places listed in The One Gold Rule.
**Do** separate surfaces on paper with 1px rules or tints, not shadows.
**Do** use the self-hosted Wittgenstein and Noto Sans, and set UI text at the 87.5% width.
**Do** let a page's brand row float over its scene when the page opens on a painted band.
**Do** write labels, errors and buttons in the product's plain voice, naming the action or the fix.
donts: **Don't** add small uppercase label lines above headings on new surfaces. Keep's four ("Chapter I · Weeks 1–4", "Main order", "Daily watch", "Hearth mission") are an exception the user approved for that screen, not a pattern to repeat.
**Don't** put drop shadows on paper surfaces, and don't use glows, gradient text, neon or game-style HUD details.
**Don't** add fake parchment texture or medieval ornament. The only picture is the painted forest.
**Don't** show points, scores, streaks or XP for faith, family or training.
**Don't** use red for anything but pain and safety states.
**Don't** add chevrons to rows that don't open anything yet.
